nota: Archived NASA data, downloaded on 2026-11-14. Daily dose = mean of absorbed_dose_rate from BioSentinel's BPD instrument, in orbit around the Sun at 1 AU (deep space, outside Earth's magnetic field). Calm reference: 6.3 µGy/h (mean of May 1-3, 2024). Level = day mean / calm: below 1.6 = 0, below 10 = 1, below 100 = 2, otherwise 3. Forecast range: made by the game from the DONKI events known that morning (flares, CMEs, particles, ENLIL runs); it is not an official NASA forecast.
instrumento: the BPD instrument on NASA's BioSentinel spacecraft, which flies around the Sun in deep space

dias.curto: No magnetic field out here, and a CME is coming!
dias.aviso: Launch success! The ship is in deep space now, far from Earth's magnetic field. At 09:12 UTC the Sun threw a CME at 1,456 km/s, and at 12:44 UTC fast particles were detected.
dias.fato: Earth's magnetic field protects astronauts on the International Space Station. On the way to Mars there is no such shield.

dias.curto: Huge X8.7 flare on the Sun!
dias.aviso: Huge flash! At 16:51 UTC the Sun fired an X8.7 flare, the strongest of the whole month.
dias.fato: BioSentinel is a small NASA spacecraft that carried yeast cells into deep space to study how radiation affects living things.

dias.aviso: Two more X flares (X3.4 at 08:37 UTC and X2.9 at 14:38 UTC).
dias.fato: Light and X-rays from a flare arrive in minutes. The fast particles can arrive minutes or hours later.

dias.curto: Solar clouds pass by. Keep the engines going!
dias.aviso: More clouds of solar material are passing by. The engines need power to reach Mars on time!
dias.fato: Water and plastic are good radiation shields because they have lots of hydrogen. Future ships may put water tanks around the crew.

dias.aviso: Mars is close! Tonight the ship must reach Mars.
dias.fato: A real trip from Earth to Mars takes about 7 months. In this game it is shortened to 5 days.
